children: Raw sugar futures on ICE rose on Wednesday, boosted partly by tight supplies in top consumer India and rising energy prices, while coffee and cocoa prices also gained.
​​settled up 0.3 cent, or 1.7%, at 18.40 cents per lb. The market set a 16-month high of 18.77 cents a week ago.
* India's port-based sugar refineries are likely to divert about 250,000 metric tons of refined sugar to the domestic market, an industry executive said on Wednesday.
* BMI analysts also said in a note that any El Nino-linked production disruptions in India would have a greater impact than in previous cycles due to low stocks.
* Oil prices jumped due to renewed attacks in the Middle East, which could give a boost to cane-based ethanol.

* Dealers said the market was supported by low exchange certified stocks.
* "Arabica certified stocks remain near their lowest level since March 1999 and likely won’t likely see a significant increase until late October, at least," Rabobank said in a note.
* Meanwhile, rains in Brazil, and forecast for more, are boosting the prospect for next year as they could improve flowering.
* "Conditions in Brazil for the 2027 crop have been excellent so far," said StoneX coffee broker Tomas Araujo.

* Ivorian cocoa traders, cooperatives and buying agents are struggling to use a new national traceability system introduced ahead of incoming European Union rules banning imports of commodities grown on recently deforested land.
